name: Timaeus
title: Father of the blind Bartimaeus
summary: Timaeus is known from the New Testament as the father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar who was healed by Jesus at Jericho. He is mentioned only indirectly through his son's name, 'Bartimaeus' (which means 'son of Timaeus'). Although little is known about Timaeus himself, his son became a witness to Jesus' healing power.

keyEvents.title: Bartimaeus mentioned as the son of Timaeus
keyEvents.description: The evangelist Mark identifies the blind beggar at Jericho as 'Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus,' which is the only reference linking Timaeus to biblical history.

keyEvents.title: Bartimaeus calls out to Jesus
keyEvents.description: Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, heard that Jesus from Nazareth was passing by and cried out: 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' His persistent faith caused Jesus to stop.

keyEvents.title: Jesus heals Bartimaeus
keyEvents.description: Jesus called Bartimaeus to him and asked what he wanted. Bartimaeus asked to receive his sight again, and Jesus healed him, saying: 'Your faith has saved you.'

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Luke
keyEvents.description: Luke also tells of the healing of a blind man at Jericho, which many scholars identify with Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, although the name is not explicitly mentioned.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Matthew
keyEvents.description: Matthew recounts the healing of two blind men at Jericho, a narrative traditionally linked to the same event where Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, was healed.
